title: Taste-Safe & Edible Sensory
strapline: Everything goes in the mouth at this age — so give the littlest explorers messy play that is meant to be tasted.
intent: Meet babies where they are: the mouth is their most sensitive research tool, so offer sensory play designed to be mouthed safely.
Give the joy and learning of messy, tactile play — squishing, smearing, grasping — without the constant 'not in your mouth'.
Build hand-eye coordination, grasp and the pincer grip through pinching, scooping and self-feeding textures.
Introduce a range of tastes, smells and temperatures — cool, warm, sweet, savoury — widening what a baby will accept.
Keep exploration calm and unhurried, with a key person close, so the sensory world feels safe as well as exciting.
implementation: Prepare taste-safe materials: plain yoghurt, mashed potato, custard, cooled cooked pasta, jelly, baby rice, soft fruit — nothing added, allergies checked with families first.
Spread it on a clean tray or highchair top and let the baby dive in with hands, feet and mouth.
Sit close and narrate the sensation ('cold and squishy — and you can taste it too!') rather than directing the play.
Colour naturally where you want colour — beetroot, spinach, turmeric — never craft dyes for the youngest mouthers.
Check every ingredient against each baby's allergy record, supervise closely, and keep textures smooth and choke-safe.
key_questions: Is the yoghurt cold on your fingers?
You tasted it — what do you think?
Can you squish it and smear it right across the tray?
Which do you like best — the smooth one or the lumpy one?
Look at the pink your fingers made in the custard!

impact.text: Babies explore edible textures with hands and mouth, mouthing and tasting to find out what each one is.
A baby scoops, pinches and self-feeds the taste-safe materials, practising the grasp that finger foods need.
Babies explore the messy materials for the pure joy of the sensation — cool, squishy, sticky, sweet.
New tastes, smells and temperatures widen what a baby will meet and accept, all through the senses.

enhancements: A naturally-coloured edible paint — yoghurt tinted with beetroot, spinach and turmeric — for the first mark-making.
A jelly dig with soft fruit set inside to find and squash.
Cooled cooked spaghetti for grasping, pulling and slurping.
A frozen-yoghurt tray on a warm day for a cool, sensory, meltable treat.
A taste-safe 'porridge' small-world with scoops, pots and spoons.

playing_exploring: The baby explores freely with hands, mouth and whole body, no wrong way to play.
Every sense is engaged — texture, taste, temperature and smell all at once.
active_learning: Babies return again and again to squish, scoop and taste, concentrating deeply on the sensation.
creating_thinking: Babies notice what their hands do to the material — smearing, mixing, making marks — and do it again.
